start.content: Peter and I fished together all night and caught nothing. Then He stood on the shore and called to us — none of us asked who He was. We simply knew. And yet I, of all people, needed to see before I could believe.

choices.text: What did you see on the shore?

doubt.content: A week after the resurrection I had said I would not believe unless I touched His wounds myself. He appeared again — and He let me touch them. 'Stop doubting and believe.' I did not need to touch anything. The sight of Him was enough.

shore_scene.content: He made a charcoal fire on the beach and invited us to breakfast. The risen Lord — cooking fish. He could have appeared in glory. He chose intimacy. After we ate, He took Peter aside, away from the rest of us.

peter_denial_context.content: Because Peter had denied Him three times. Three times, beside a charcoal fire very much like this one. He needed a restoration that matched the weight of the failure — not one question, but three.

peter_commission.content: Three times He asked: 'Do you love me?' Three times Peter answered yes. Three times He said: 'Feed my sheep.' Peter wept on the third question. We all understood — this was not interrogation. This was grace, precisely calibrated to undo a precise wound.

closing.content: Restored and commissioned. He told Peter to follow Him — the same two words He used at the very beginning beside the Sea of Galilee. Three years, a death, a resurrection, and it ends with the same invitation. Follow me. I think that is the point.
